subproblem.title: Real-analysis rigidity: an α-independent, degree-one homogeneous density on a box is c·t
subproblem.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ 1 and let H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ be integrable on O_s := (1 − s, 1 + s) × (−s, s) (Lebesgue measure). Assume (α) ∫_{ℝ×ℝ} ψ'(α)·l(t)·H(t, α) d(t, α) = 0 for all ψ, l ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport ψ ⊆ (−s, s) and tsupport l ⊆ (1 − s, 1 + s); and (β) ∫ l(t/r)·ψ(α)·H(t, α) d(t, α) = r²·∫ l(t)·ψ(α)·H(t, α) d(t, α) for all l, ψ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with tsupport l ⊆ (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2), tsupport ψ ⊆ (−s, s), and every r ∈ ℝ with |r − 1| < s/4. Then there is c ∈ ℝ with H(t, α) = c·t for almost every (t, α) ∈ (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8) × (−s, s).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 8 (H depends only on t) and 9(b) (h(t) = ct), with s_1 := s/4 and s_2 := s/8. Notation: I := (1 − s, 1 + s), I' := (−s, s), O := O_s = I × I'; Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ is the product measure (Fubini–Tonelli).
0. (Supports.) In (α) the integrand vanishes off O and is bounded by sup|ψ'|·sup|l|·|H| on O, so it is integrable and its integral is the integral over O. In (β), |r − 1| < s/4 ≤ 1/4 gives r > 0, and if l(t/r) ≠ 0 then t ∈ (r(1 − s/2), r(1 + s/2)) ⊆ I, because (1 − s/4)(1 − s/2) = 1 − 3s/4 + s²/8 > 1 − s and (1 + s/4)(1 + s/2) = 1 + 3s/4 + s²/8 ≤ 1 + 7s/8 < 1 + s (s² ≤ s); likewise l(t) ≠ 0 implies t ∈ I. So both integrands in (β) are supported in O and integrable.
1. (Measurable version.) H is a.e.-strongly measurable on O; let H̃ be Borel with H̃ = H a.e. on O and H̃ := 0 off O. H̃ is integrable on ℝ × ℝ, and (α), (β) and the conclusion are unchanged when H is replaced by H̃ (all integrands are supported in O, and the conclusion is an a.e. statement on a subset of O). By Fubini, for a.e. t ∈ I the function H̃(t, ·) is integrable on I', and for bounded Borel b, l the function t ↦ ∫_{I'} b(α)H̃(t, α) dα is integrable on I with ∫_I l(t)(∫_{I'} b(α)H̃(t, α) dα) dt = ∫_O l(t)b(α)H̃(t, α) d(t, α).
2. (For each ψ, the α-integral vanishes for a.e. t.) Fix ψ ∈ C¹ with tsupport ψ ⊆ I' and put Φ_ψ(t) := ∫_{I'} ψ'(α)H̃(t, α) dα (integrable on I by step 1). By (α) and Fubini, ∫_I l(t)Φ_ψ(t) dt = 0 for every l ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with compact support in I (C^∞ ⊆ C¹). By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib `IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero` on the open set I, Φ_ψ being locally integrable on I), Φ_ψ(t) = 0 for a.e. t ∈ I.
3. (A countable dense family.) For j ∈ ℕ with 1/j < s let S_j := {ψ ∈ C¹(ℝ) : ψ = 0 outside [−s + 1/j, s − 1/j]}. The map ψ ↦ (ψ|_{[−s,s]}, ψ'|_{[−s,s]}) is injective on S_j into C([−s, s]) × C([−s, s]), a separable metric space (continuous functions on a compact metric space; Mathlib `ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace`, C(X, Y) is separable for X second countable and locally compact and Y second countable, and on the compact X = [−s, s] the compact-open topology is the topology of uniform convergence), and subsets of separable metric spaces are separable; so there is a countable D_j ⊆ S_j such that every ψ ∈ S_j is the limit of some ψ_i ∈ D_j with ψ_i → ψ and ψ_i' → ψ' uniformly on [−s, s] (all ψ_i vanish outside [−s + 1/j, s − 1/j]). Let D_0 := ⋃_j D_j (countable). Every ψ ∈ C¹ with tsupport ψ ⊆ I' lies in some S_j, since tsupport ψ is a compact subset of the open interval I'.
4. (For a.e. t, all ψ.) By steps 1–3 there is a null set N_0 ⊆ I such that for t ∈ I ∖ N_0: H̃(t, ·) is integrable on I' and Φ_ψ(t) = 0 for all ψ ∈ D_0. For such t and any ψ ∈ C¹ with tsupport ψ ⊆ I', take ψ_i ∈ D_j → ψ as in step 3; then |ψ_i'(α)H̃(t, α)| ≤ (sup|ψ'| + 1)|H̃(t, α)| for large i and ψ_i' → ψ' pointwise, so by dominated convergence Φ_ψ(t) = lim Φ_{ψ_i}(t) = 0.
5. (One-dimensional constancy.) Fix t ∈ I ∖ N_0 and let u(α) := H̃(t, α) for α ∈ I', u := 0 elsewhere. Let ι : ℝ → Euclid 1 be the linear isometry α ↦ α·e_0 (it preserves Lebesgue measure) and U := ι(I'), open and convex, hence preconnected. For φ ∈ C¹(Euclid 1) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ U, ψ := φ∘ι is C¹ with tsupport ψ ⊆ I' and Dφ(ια)(e_0) = ψ'(α); hence ∫ (u∘ι⁻¹)(z)·Dφ(z)(e_0) dz = ∫ u(α)ψ'(α) dα = Φ_ψ(t) = 0. By SimonGMT `ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero` (n = 1, f := u∘ι⁻¹, which is locally integrable on U) there is c_t with u = c_t a.e. on I'. So H̃(t, α) = c_t for a.e. α ∈ I', and c_t = h(t) := (2s)⁻¹∫_{I'} H̃(t, α) dα.
6. (H̃ = h(t) on O.) h is Borel and integrable on I (Fubini). The set B := {(t, α) ∈ O : H̃(t, α) ≠ h(t)} is Borel, and for a.e. t its t-section is null (step 5); by Tonelli (`Measure.measure_prod_null`) B is null. So H̃(t, α) = h(t) for a.e. (t, α) ∈ O.
7. (Scaling identity for h.) Fix ψ_0 ∈ C^∞ with tsupport ψ_0 ⊆ I' and ∫ψ_0 = 1 (a normalized smooth bump centred at 0). For l ∈ C^∞ with tsupport l ⊆ I_1 := (1 − s/2, 1 + s/2) and |r − 1| < s/4, steps 0, 6 and Fubini give ∫ l(t/r)ψ_0(α)H̃ = ∫_I l(t/r)h(t) dt and ∫ l(t)ψ_0(α)H̃ = ∫_I l(t)h(t) dt, so by (β), ∫ l(t/r)h(t) dt = r²∫ l(u)h(u) du. Substituting t = ru (r > 0): ∫ l(t/r)h(t) dt = r∫ l(u)h(ru) du. Hence ∫ l(u)(h(ru) − r·h(u)) du = 0 for all such l (u ↦ h(ru) is integrable on I_1 because rI_1 ⊆ I). By the fundamental lemma on the open interval I_1, h(ru) = r·h(u) for a.e. u ∈ I_1, for each r with |r − 1| < s/4.
8. (Homogeneity.) Let s_1 := s/4, so I_1 = (1 − 2s_1, 1 + 2s_1), and put g(u) := h(u)/u (Borel on I). The Borel function Δ(u, r) := g(ru) − g(u) on I_1 × (1 − s_1, 1 + s_1) has null u-sections for every r (step 7), so by Tonelli Δ = 0 a.e. on the product, and by Tonelli in the other order, for a.e. u ∈ I_1, g(ru) = g(u) for a.e. r ∈ (1 − s_1, 1 + s_1). The interval (1 − s_1/4, 1 + s_1/4) ⊆ I_1 has positive measure, so choose u_0 in it with this property and put c := g(u_0). Since r ↦ ru_0 is an affine bijection (u_0 > 0) mapping null sets to null sets, g(v) = c for a.e. v ∈ (u_0(1 − s_1), u_0(1 + s_1)). As u_0(1 − s_1) < (1 + s_1/4)(1 − s_1) < 1 − s_1/2 and u_0(1 + s_1) > (1 − s_1/4)(1 + s_1) > 1 + s_1/2 (0 < s_1 ≤ 1/4), we get h(v) = c·v for a.e. v ∈ (1 − s_1/2, 1 + s_1/2) = (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8).
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 1, 6 and 8, H(t, α) = H̃(t, α) = h(t) = c·t for a.e. (t, α) ∈ (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8) × (−s, s) (a product of a null set of t-values with I' is null). ∎

For each ψ, t ↦ ∫ψ'(α)H̃(t,α)dα integrates to 0 against all l ∈ C^∞_c(I), so it vanishes a.e.
A countable C¹-dense family of ψ (separability) gives: for a.e. t, ∫ψ'(α)H̃(t,α)dα = 0 for every ψ ∈ C¹_c(I').

(β) with a normalized ψ_0 gives h(ru) = r h(u) a.e. for each r; Fubini in (u, r) gives h(v)/v constant a.e. near 1, so H = ct on (1 − s/8, 1 + s/8) × (−s, s).

subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) (C : GeometricCurrentOn univ 2, ℝ^P = Euclid P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ) with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). Then for every y ∈ spt C and every ρ > 0, ω_2·ρ² ≤ M_{B_ρ(y)}(C), i.e. unitBallVolume 2 * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ 2) ≤ C.massOn (ball y ρ).

Its hypotheses hold: 1 ≤ 2 ≤ P ≤ P (step 1); univ is open; IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 P univ holds with the identity chart (for each point take V := W := univ ⊆ Euclid P and ψ := id: id is C^∞ and injective, id '' univ = univ ∩ univ, V ∩ id⁻¹(K) = K is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and fderiv ℝ id z = id is injective); (closure univ ∖ univ) ∩ univ = ∅; IsMinimizingIn C (univ ∩ univ) because univ ∩ univ = univ; spt C ⊆ univ ∩ univ; BoundaryVanishes C. subproblem.title: On the planar sector, almost every point lies in the carrier with multiplicity k and tangent plane Q
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P), Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, and assume that for all t > 0 and φ ∈ (0, δ) the point y := t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e) satisfies HasMassDensity C y k and spt C ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ Q for some r > 0. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, 2) represent C. Then for Lebesgue-almost every p = (t, α) ∈ ℝ × ℝ with t > 0, 0 < α < δ and α < 1, the point x_Q(p) := t(cos α·a + sin α·e) satisfies x_Q(p) ∈ M, θ(x_Q(p)) = k and approxTangentPlane 2 M x_Q(p) = Q.

Let δ_1 := min(δ, 1), Π(t, φ) := t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e) = ι(κ⁻¹(polarCoord.symm(t, φ))) (polarCoord.symm(t, φ) = (t cos φ, t sin φ)), and S := Π((0, ∞) × (0, δ_1)) ⊆ Q.
1. (S is open in Q; local planarity.) polarCoord.symm maps (0, ∞) × (−π, π) homeomorphically onto ℝ × ℝ minus the closed half-line (−∞, 0] × {0}, an open set, and (0, ∞) × (0, δ_1) is an open subset of (0, ∞) × (−π, π) (δ_1 ≤ 1 < π); κ⁻¹ and ι are homeomorphisms onto Euclid 2 and Q; so S is open in Q. 4. (Polar coordinates.) Choose a Borel S' ⊇ S_bad with H²(S') = 0 (MeasureTheory.exists_measurable_superset_of_null) and let B := κ(ι⁻¹(S')) ⊆ ℝ × ℝ, Borel (κ and ι are homeomorphisms onto their ranges) with Lebesgue(B) = Lebesgue_{Euclid 2}(ι⁻¹(S')) = H²(ι(ι⁻¹(S'))) ≤ H²(S') = 0. subproblem.title: Integrality of fibre multiplicities: k ≤ m, and k < m forces excess mass in the small boxes
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), with ∂C = 0 and a cone (IsConeCurrent C). Let Q be a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1. Assume a ∈ spt C and that for all t > 0 and φ ∈ (0, δ) the point y := t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e) satisfies HasMassDensity C y k and spt C ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ Q for some r > 0. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of C, μ := R.measure, m ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C a m, and 0 < s ≤ 1/4 such that the localization property Loc(s) holds: for every s' ∈ (0, s] and every x ∈ spt C with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s' and |x − πx| ≤ 2s|x| one has |x − πx| < (s'/4)|x| and |x − a| < 3s' (π := Q.starProjection, f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)). For s' > 0 let Z(s, s') := {x : ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|}. Then k ≤ m, and if k < m there is s₃ > 0 such that (4m + 2)·s'²·(1 − 2s') ≤ μ(Z(s, s')) (as ENNReal.ofReal of the left side) for every s' ∈ (0, s₃].

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 11 and 12 (fibre inequalities and integrality). Conventions: H² := μHE[2]; μ = θ·H²⌞M, θ ≥ 1 on M, so H²(M ∩ S) ≤ μ(S) for Borel S and μ ≪ H²⌞M; q(x) := x − πx; Ax := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a; Ω := {⟨x,a⟩ > 0}; T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x, p_{T_x} its orthogonal projection; w(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|, G(x) := w(x)²/|πx|², J(x) := w(x)/|πx|²; Z(s,s') := {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |q(x)| < s|x|}, Z := Z(s,s); F̃(x) := (|x|, f(x)); fibre X(p) := M ∩ Z ∩ F̃⁻¹{p}, H(p) := Σ_{x∈X(p)} θ(x)w(x), N(p) := Σ_{x∈X(p)} θ(x) (tsums in [0, ∞]). (F1) (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, πx = ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e. (F2) A is linear with values in Q, ⟨Ax, x⟩ = 0, |Ax| = |πx|, so w ≤ |πx| ≤ |x|, πx ≠ 0 on Ω and 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 there. (F3) On Ω, f is C^∞, |f| < π/2, f(rx) = f(x) (r > 0), and πx = |πx|(cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e). (Supp) spt C = μ.support (`Submission.imrep_represents_support_eq_inter_measure_support`, U = univ) and μ((spt C)ᶜ) = 0 (`MeasureTheory.Measure.support_mem_ae`; ℝ^P is second countable). (Uniq) HasMassDensity C a θ and HasMassDensity C a θ' imply θ = θ'. x_Q(p) := p_1(cos p_2·a + sin p_2·e) for p = (p_1, p_2).
0. (Inputs.) Sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_cone_stationary_radial`: p_{T_x}x = x for μ-a.e. x. Sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_flux_density_eq` (same hypotheses): s₂ > 0 with H(p) = ofReal(m·p_1) for a.e. p ∈ Box(s₂) := (1 − s₂, 1 + s₂) × (−s₂, s₂). Sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_sector_carrier_points`: for a.e. p with p_1 > 0, 0 < p_2 < δ and p_2 < 1, x_Q(p) ∈ M, θ(x_Q(p)) = k and T_{x_Q(p)} = Q. Sibling `Submission.idtp_cse_fibre_area_identities` (radial tangency): ∫ b·N = ∫_Z b(F̃(x))·J(x) dμ for measurable b ≥ 0. Put s₃ := min(s₂, δ/2, s/2) > 0; note s₃ ≤ 1/8.
1. (Geometry of fibres.) Let p = (t, α) with |t − 1| < s and |α| < s (so t > 0 and |α| < 1/4 < π/2). (i) x_Q(p) ∈ Z and F̃(x_Q(p)) = p: |x_Q(p)| = t (a ⊥ e unit), ⟨x_Q(p), a⟩ = t cos α > 0, f(x_Q(p)) = arctan(t sin α/(t cos α)) = arctan(tan α) = α, and q(x_Q(p)) = 0 < s·t since x_Q(p) ∈ Q. (ii) Every x ∈ X(p) has |x| = t and w(x) ≤ |Ax| = |πx| ≤ t; if x ≠ x_Q(p) then |πx| < t and so w(x) < t. Indeed, if |πx| = |x| then |q(x)|² = |x|² − |πx|² = 0, x = πx ∈ Q, and by (F3) x = πx = |πx|(cos f(x)·a + sin f(x)·e) = t(cos α·a + sin α·e) = x_Q(p). (iii) If x_Q(p) ∈ M and T_{x_Q(p)} = Q, then x_Q(p) ∈ X(p) by (i), and w(x_Q(p)) = |p_Q(Ax_Q(p))| = |Ax_Q(p)| = |πx_Q(p)| = t (A takes values in Q). (iv) ofReal(t)·N(p) ≥ H(p): termwise θ(x)·ofReal(w(x)) ≤ θ(x)·ofReal(t) by (ii), and ENNReal.tsum_mul_left.
2. (Good set.) Let G_1 be the set of p ∈ Box(s₃) with H(p) = ofReal(m·p_1) and such that, if p_2 > 0, x_Q(p) ∈ M, θ(x_Q(p)) = k and T_{x_Q(p)} = Q. Since Box(s₃) ⊆ Box(s₂) and p ∈ Box(s₃) with p_2 > 0 has p_1 > 0, p_2 < s₃ ≤ δ/2 < δ and p_2 < 1, step 0 shows that a.e. p ∈ Box(s₃) lies in G_1. Points of Box(s₃) satisfy |p_1 − 1| < s and |p_2| < s, so step 1 applies to them.
3. (k ≤ m.) Suppose k > m. The set {p ∈ G_1 : p_2 > 0} has positive measure (its complement in (1 − s₃, 1 + s₃) × (0, s₃) is null). For such p = (t, α), by 1(iii) the term of x_Q(p) in H(p) is θ(x_Q(p))·ofReal(t) = k·ofReal(t), so H(p) ≥ k·ofReal(t) > m·ofReal(t) = ofReal(m t) = H(p) (t > 0, k > m), a contradiction. Hence k ≤ m.
4. (Lower bounds for N.) For p = (t, α) ∈ G_1: by 1(iv), ofReal(t)·N(p) ≥ ofReal(m t), so N(p) ≥ m. Assume now k < m and α > 0; we show N(p) ≥ m + 1. If N(p) = ∞ this is clear. Otherwise X(p) is finite (θ ≥ 1 on M, so a finite sum Σθ has finitely many nonzero terms), x_Q(p) ∈ X(p) by 1(iii), and with X'(p) := X(p) ∖ {x_Q(p)}, N'(p) := Σ_{X'(p)} θ and H'(p) := Σ_{X'(p)} θ·ofReal(w): N(p) = k + N'(p) and H(p) = k·ofReal(t) + H'(p). As H(p) = ofReal(m t) is finite, H'(p) = ofReal((m − k)t) > 0, so X'(p) ≠ ∅; each x ∈ X'(p) has w(x) < t (1(ii)) and θ(x) ≥ 1, so H'(p) < ofReal(t)·N'(p) (finite nonempty sum of strict inequalities). Hence (m − k)t < t·N'(p), N'(p) > m − k, and as N'(p) and m − k are integers, N'(p) ≥ m − k + 1, i.e. N(p) ≥ m + 1.
5. (Integral lower bound.) Assume k < m and let 0 < s' ≤ s₃, Sq(s') := (1 − s', 1 + s') × (−s', s') ⊆ Box(s₃). By step 4, a.e. on Sq(s'): N ≥ m + 1_{p_2 > 0}. Hence ∫_{Sq(s')} N ≥ m·4s'² + 2s'² = (4m + 2)s'² (as ENNReal.ofReal).
6. (Integral upper bound.) By step 0 with b := 1_{Sq(s')}: ∫_{Sq(s')} N = ∫_{Z ∩ F̃⁻¹(Sq(s'))} J dμ = ∫_{Z(s,s')} J dμ (s' ≤ s, so Z ∩ F̃⁻¹(Sq(s')) = Z(s, s')). For x ∈ spt C ∩ Z(s, s'), Loc(s) (applicable since |q(x)| < s|x| ≤ 2s|x|) gives |q(x)| < (s'/4)|x|, so |πx| ≥ |x| − |q(x)| > (1 − s'/4)(1 − s') ≥ 1 − 2s' > 0 (s' ≤ 1/8), and J(x) = w(x)/|πx|² ≤ 1/|πx| ≤ 1/(1 − 2s') (w ≤ |πx|). By (Supp), ∫_{Z(s,s')} J dμ ≤ ofReal(1/(1 − 2s'))·μ(Z(s, s')).
7. (Conclusion.) For 0 < s' ≤ s₃: ofReal((4m + 2)s'²) ≤ ofReal(1/(1 − 2s'))·μ(Z(s, s')); multiplying by ofReal(1 − 2s') > 0 gives ofReal((4m + 2)s'²(1 − 2s')) ≤ μ(Z(s, s')). Together with step 3 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Inputs: H = mt a.e. near (1,0) (sibling flux_density), sector points x_Q(t,α) ∈ M with θ = k and T = Q (sibling sector_points), and the N-identity (sibling fibre_area).
Fibre geometry: x_Q(t,α) is the only point of Q in the fibre, it carries weight w = t, and all other fibre points have w < t.
k > m would give H ≥ kt > mt on the sector side, so k ≤ m.
If k < m, integrality of θ gives N ≥ m + 1 on the sector side and N ≥ m elsewhere, so ∫_{Sq(s')} N ≥ (4m + 2)s'².
